title: Closed-loop KPI Runway & Stakeholder Rhythm (beta→scale)
content:
Context:
This is a working playbook and tracker for taking features from private beta through an intentional, closed-loop scaling rhythm. Purpose is to align Product Ops, Product Managers, Eng, SRE and GTM with a single KPI runway + stakeholder cadence so decisions are evidence-led and fast.

High-level approach (GPS + Compass metaphor):
- GPS: weekly quantitative telemetry snapshots (what the numbers say). Short, repeatable dataset we can compute automatically.
- Compass: qualitative signals from stakeholders (support, sales, customer feedback, PM notes). A short rubric that converts voice into a signal: green/amber/red with a 1–2 sentence rationale.
- Closed-loop cadence: feed GPS+Compass into a weekly Quick-Stand decision (15–30 min) and a bi-weekly Ops Review (45–60 min) for deeper tradeoffs.

Minimal KPI runway (compute every 24h stacked into weekly windows):
- Primary adoption KPI: active-engaged-users-per-day (AEU) — definition: unique users with >=2 successful feature interactions in 24h. Target: grow from beta baseline -> +20% week-over-week for initial 4 weeks.
- Cost per successful inference (CPSI) — definition: total inference spend / successful interactions. Guardrail: CPSI <= $0.10 in beta; target reduction via batching/quantization to $0.04 by scale.
- Latency P95 (end-to-end) — definition: request->final-token response P95. SLO: < 350ms. Threshold: > 500ms triggers amber.
- Failure rate (errors that impact UX) — definition: 4xx/5xx or exporter-detected malformed responses / total requests. Threshold: >1.5% → amber, >4% → red.
- Quality regression score (QRS) — definition: automatic eval delta on representative prompt suite, sampled at 500 calls/week. Acceptable drift: <= 2% change in top-level metric.

Compass (qualitative rubric, weekly):
- Support signal: trending increase in tickets labeled with feature_name (compare 7d vs 7d prior).
- Sales/CS feedback: number of active deals where feature cited as blocker/opportunity.
- PM judgement: PM assigns contextual risk (low/med/high) tied to specific hypotheses.
- Customer quotes: 3 anonymized representative quotes each week (positive/negative).

Signal enrichment process (how to turn data into decisions):
1) Automation collects GPS metrics every 24h and writes to shared chart (data team pipeline: dataset id PRODOPS.runway_daily).
2) Support bot tags tickets and surfaces top-3 triage issues in the weekly note.
3) Ops lead synthesizes Compass inputs and proposes 1 recommendation in the Quick-Stand.

Weekly Quick-Stand (15–30 min):
- Inputs: 1-pager (1 slide) snapshot containing the five runway KPIs and Compass flags.
- Decision outcomes: "stay beta", "incremental rollout +10% traffic", "scale" or "rollback to frozen". Each outcome must have an owner and an ETA.

Bi-weekly Ops Review (45–60 min):
- Deep dive on anomalies (latency, cost spikes, quality regressions).
- Decide on experiments (e.g., routing to cheaper model variants, adjust batching, prompt tweaks, safety hold).
- Commit to runway changes and operational interventions.

Go/No-go checklist (for each incremental rollout step):
- Telemetry green on Primary adoption KPI (>= baseline +20% WoW) or explicit PM rationale for exception.
- CPSI within guardrail for proposed traffic delta.
- Latency P95 within SLO or mitigation plan with timelines (owner + ETA).
- No active customer-security/legal issues (security sign-off present).
- Runbook for rollback published and smoke-tests automated.
- On-call rota includes SRE + Product Ops + PM contact for 72h after rollout.

Escalation matrix (if any step triggers amber/red):
- Amber: Ops Lead + PM notified in Quick-Stand. Owner assigned to a 24h action item.
- Red: Pager to SRE oncall, PM, Head of Product Ops + Exec sponsor. Emergency rollback evaluated within 60 minutes.

Owner mapping (single-line owners for automation):
- Data pipeline & daily charts: Ethan Brooks
- Support tagging & ticket feed: Amit Patel
- Quality eval suite maintenance: Sofia Martinez
- Runbook + rollout coordination: Maya Chen (Product Ops)

Lightweight templates (copy/paste into the weekly shared note):
- Snapshot header (one-liner): "Week W — AEU: 1,324 (+18% WoW) | CPSI: $0.072 | Latency P95: 312ms (green) | Fail rate: 0.9% (green) | QRS delta: -0.4% (stable)"
- Compass line: "Support: amber — surge in ticket tag 'edge-case-X' (12->38). Sales: green — 2 deals referenced. PM: low risk (hypothesis being validated). Quote: 'response sometimes returns hallucinated steps'"
- Proposed action (one sentence): "Increase canary traffic +10% for 48h with active SRE watch; open hotfix ticket for 'edge-case-X'. Owner: DevTeamAlpha; ETA: 24h"

Launch readiness artifacts to attach before any +traffic action: (checkboxes for the tracker)
- [ ] Canary routing configured & smoke tests passing (link to smoke run)
- [ ] Rollback playbook published & tested (link)
- [ ] Billing alert thresholds set (CPSI threshold alert)
- [ ] Latency alarms created (P95/P99) and routed to oncall
- [ ] Quality eval runner gated (automated nightly run green)
- [ ] Security & legal signoff doc attached
- [ ] Communications plan for customers (template included)

Experimental knobs (ops playbook snippets):
- Batching window: test 20ms -> 80ms -> 200ms for cost vs latency tradeoffs; measure CPSI and P95 at each step.
- Quantization profile: A/B two quantization levels with traffic split 5/95 for 48 hours.
- Fallback routing: live traffic fallback to smaller/verified model when latency > threshold for 2 consecutive 5-min buckets.

Operational notes and gotchas (lessons learned):
- Don’t treat adoption % as only signal — small cohorts can hide regressions; always cross-check quality eval deltas.
- Batch increases are highly model-dependent; measure P99 — P95 alone can mask tail latency issues.
- Keep CPSI math transparent: include infra credits, storage costs and batching overheads.

Next actions (short):
- Finalize automation deck for daily GPS (Ethan) — due 2024-11-10.
- Runbook dry-run with SRE on 2024-11-12 (Maya + SRE rota).
- PMs to nominate 3 representative prompts for QRS eval by 2024-11-08 (Sofia).

Relevant links and quick references:
- Confluence: PRODOPS-Runway-Compass (synthesis + dashboards)
- Jira: PRODOPS-4217 (runway automation epic), PS-1902 (smoke test coverage)
- Slack thread: #prodops-runway (pin: weekly snapshot)

Appendix: quick one-page example of a green->amber->red sequence and decision log (short):
- Day 1: Canary +10% — AEUs rise 12% (green), CPSI +8% (amber) due to small batch misconfiguration -> Ops lead orders batching rollback.
- Day 2: Batch rollback -> CPSI restored, latency stable (green) -> decision: resume +10% with corrected batch settings.

Comments / requests for reviewers:
- Are the CPSI guardrails realistic? PMs: please review cost baseline assumptions for your verticals.
- SREs: are the latency thresholds sufficient for our SLA commitments or too optimistic?
- Sales/CS: is the Compass rubric capturing the most useful GTM signals?

(End of working doc — please make copies for individual projects; this file is the canonical closed-loop runway template for product ops.)
